cues.zh: 大家好，我是 Casey Muratori。
cues.en: Hey everybody, Casey Muratori here.

cues.zh: 在 Molly Rocket，我们做了一部很酷的图像小说系列，叫 Meow the Infinite，
cues.en: At Molly Rocket, we do a cool graphic novel series called Meow the Infinite,

cues.zh: 讲的是太空里的猫，还有很多别的东西。
cues.en: about cats in space and a lot of other stuff.

cues.zh: 我们很想寄一本 Meow the Infinite 给你，所以现在正在办 Kickstarter。
cues.en: We would love to send you a copy of Meow the Infinite, which is why we're running a Kickstarter right now.

cues.zh: 链接在下方说明里，
cues.en: The link is in the description below,

cues.zh: 我们正在做印刷版。
cues.en: and we're doing a print run.

cues.zh: 很希望你能参与进来。
cues.en: We'd love for you to be a part of it.

cues.zh: 如果有机会去看看，请一定去。
cues.en: If you get a chance to check that out, please do.

cues.zh: 作为 Kickstarter 宣传的一部分，我在做一系列编程直播，讲一些我早就想覆盖的编程主题，
cues.en: As part of the promotion for the Kickstarter, I'm doing a bunch of programming streams where I go over programming topics that I've been meaning to cover for a while,

cues.zh: 只是一直没时间做。
cues.en: and just hadn't had the time to do.

cues.zh: 我刚做了一期讲 Refterm 的。
cues.en: I just did one on Refterm.

cues.zh: 这是我写的一个程序，目的是证明终端性能可以比我们习惯的高出一百倍甚至一千倍。
cues.en: This is a program that I wrote that was designed to show that terminal performance could be increased by a hundred or a thousand times over what we're used to.

cues.zh: 其实，与其说它关乎终端，不如说它关乎一般的软件开发实践。
cues.en: And really, it wasn't so much about terminals as it was about software development practices in general.

cues.zh: 为什么明明不必慢，事情却还是这么慢？
cues.en: Why are things so slow when they don't have to be?

cues.zh: 所以这只是给出一个具体例子：你看，当大家说软件真的很慢时，
cues.en: And so it's just to provide a single specific example of, look, when folks say that software is really slow,

cues.zh: 他们真不是开玩笑。
cues.en: they're not kidding.

cues.zh: 它本可以有多快。
cues.en: Here's how fast it could be.

cues.zh: 那场直播本身大概有五个小时。
cues.en: The live stream itself was like five hours long.

cues.zh: 所以我把它拆成了若干片段，每段讲一个具体内容。
cues.en: So what I've done is I've broken it up into chunks that each cover a specific thing.

cues.zh: 这是关于优化哲学的第一部分，只是为后面讲我如何看待人们做软件开发的方式做个铺垫。
cues.en: This is part one about the philosophy of optimization, and it's just here to set the stage for how I think about the way people approach software development.

cues.zh: 希望你喜欢。
cues.en: I hope you enjoy it.

cues.zh: 在现代编程的各种问题中，我会说优化很可能排在最最最前面。
cues.en: Of the things that are a problem in modern programming, I would say that optimization is probably at the very, very, very top of the list.

cues.zh: 我之所以这么说，是因为虽然我不能说已有实证分析
cues.en: And the reason that I say that is because although I can't say that there's empirical analysis

cues.zh: 来支持这一点，因为我们这些年根本没持续收集数据，
cues.en: to support this because we simply haven't been collecting data across the years,

cues.zh: 但我会说，在当今这个时代，我们实际利用现有计算机硬件来解决目标问题的程度，处于历史最低点。
cues.en: I would say that in today's day and age, the degree to which we're able to actually use the computer hardware we have to solve the problems we're trying to solve is at an all-time low.

cues.zh: 亲身经历过那个时代，我根本不觉得我在 Commodore 64 或 Amiga 3000 上跑的大多数东西
cues.en: Having lived through it, I don't fundamentally believe that most of the things I ran on my Commodore 64 or my Amiga 3000

cues.zh: 会比硬件本可以运行它们的速度慢上一百倍或一千倍。
cues.en: were running a hundred or a thousand times slower than the hardware was capable of running them.

cues.zh: 但今天，我用的大多数软件大致就在这个量级。
cues.en: But today, most software I use is roughly in that ballpark.

cues.zh: 我会说，它大约慢了 100 到 1000 倍
cues.en: I would say it's somewhere between 100 and 1,000 times slower

cues.zh: 比它本可以达到的速度。
cues.en: than what it could be doing.

cues.zh: 而且这个问题如此普遍，却似乎没让大家多在意，以至于我们都没采取激烈措施去纠正它，
cues.en: And the fact that that's so endemic and also that it doesn't seem to concern people very much such that we're not taking drastic action to correct it,

cues.zh: 这让我觉得，我们面临一个相当严重的问题。
cues.en: suggests to me that we have a pretty serious problem.

cues.zh: 显然，我们没有财务问题，因为我们照样能拿到报酬，
cues.en: Now, obviously we don't have a financial problem because we still are getting paid just fine,

cues.zh: 呃，不管我们做不做优化。
cues.en: uh, whether we're doing optimization or not.

cues.zh: 所以我说我们有问题时，绝不是指有人明天会拿不到钱，
cues.en: So when I say we have a problem, I certainly don't mean that anyone's going to not get paid

cues.zh: 就因为他们没做优化。
cues.en: tomorrow because they're not optimizing.

cues.zh: 但我的意思是，如果我们想以前瞻性的方式看待这个职业，想弄清：既然社会确实付给计算机行业很多钱，我们怎样才能为整个社会交付更好的价值，
cues.en: But what I mean is, if we want to look at our profession in a forward-thinking way, and we want to say how can we deliver a better value, uh, to society as a whole for paying us, because they certainly do pay the computer industry a lot of money,

cues.zh: 未来我们怎样才能做得更好，交付的软件质量能配得上所交付硬件的质量？
cues.en: how can we do a better job in the future at delivering software that lives up to the quality of the hardware that's being delivered?

cues.zh: 除此之外，我不是搞硬件的人，所以我不知道，也许硬件也很糟糕，但我说不准。
cues.en: And separate from that, I'm not a hardware person, so I don't know, maybe the hardware is terrible too, but I couldn't tell you.

cues.zh: 我完全不知道。
cues.en: I have no idea.

cues.zh: 我只知道软件非常非常慢。
cues.en: All I know is that the software is very, very slow.

cues.zh: 所以，
cues.en: So,

cues.zh: 在这个系列里，我想聊的，呃，就是优化的哲学。
cues.en: what I wanted to talk about, uh, in this series is just the philosophies of optimization.

cues.zh: 我认为大概有三种。
cues.en: I see there as being roughly three of them.

cues.zh: 我想用我最近做的那个终端参考渲染器来举例，因为它的代码库非常简单，它能说明大多数终端程序
cues.en: And I wanted to use the reference renderer for terminals that I did recently because it's a very simple code base, and it shows how most terminal programs

cues.zh: 比它们本该有的速度慢了一百到一千倍。
cues.en: are about a hundred to a thousand times slower than they should be.

cues.zh: 我想解释一下，优化的哲学大概是什么，我做那个东西时用的是哪一种，嗯，因为我觉得这一点也很重要。
cues.en: And I wanted to explain, you know, kind of what philosophies of optimization are, which one I used when I was making that, um, because I think that's important as well.

cues.zh: 然后也许过一遍代码库，展示一下为什么我觉得我们没必要地陷到了这么
cues.en: And then maybe go through the code base to just sort of show why I think we're sort of unnecessarily so far down

cues.zh: 这种糟糕的、十万倍变慢的阶段。
cues.en: this sort of, uh, nasty 100,000x, uh, slow down phase of things.

cues.zh: 所以优化的理念是，
cues.en: So the philosophies of optimization are,

cues.zh: 你可能会笑，但我真的觉得有三种。
cues.en: and you're going to laugh, but I honestly think there's three.

cues.zh: 第一种是优化。
cues.en: Number one is optimization.

cues.zh: 这种理念是，我们确实要对代码做一些优化。
cues.en: This philosophy is that we're actually going to do some optimization on the code.

cues.zh: 我们要看看现有硬件运行某段代码应该能有多快。
cues.en: We're going to look to see how fast the hardware we have should be able to run a particular piece of code.

cues.zh: 我们会，呃，这基于查看代码必须执行的操作，嗯，还涉及检查算法，确保这个算法……
cues.en: We're going, you know, and this is based on looking at the operations that that code has to do, um, it involves looking at the algorithm to make sure that the algorithm is such that it,

cues.zh: 它不会做明显浪费的事，也不会是不必要的高阶复杂度，比如本该是 O 的时候却不是平方复杂度，诸如此类。
cues.en: you know, isn't doing things that are obviously wasteful or isn't an unnecessarily order that's too high, like it's it's not squared when it should be O and, things like that.

cues.zh: 然后我们会看看，计算机执行得出结果所需的数学运算能有多快。
cues.en: Then we're going to look at how fast the computer can do the required mathematical operations necessary to produce the result.

cues.zh: 我们会给代码做基准测试，看看它和理论最大吞吐量相比如何。
cues.en: We're going to benchmark our code and see how it compares to those theoretical maximum throughput numbers.

cues.zh: 然后，如果我们发现代码性能没达到预期水平，就会收集性能数据，
cues.en: Um, and then to the extent that we find that our code is not performing up to the level that we think it should, we are going to collect performance data

cues.zh: 比如 CPU 的性能计数器、计时数据之类，试着找出我们对它运行速度的理解
cues.en: such as performance counters from the CPU, timings, those sorts of things, to try and isolate where our understanding of how fast this runs

cues.zh: 在哪里偏离了软件在 CPU 上实际运行的情况。
cues.en: deviates from the actual in practice, uh, running of the the software on the CPU.

cues.zh: 这就是优化。
cues.en: That's optimization.

cues.zh: 这是一种极少数人会实践的哲学，包括我自己在内。
cues.en: That's a philosophy practiced by very, very few people, including myself,

cues.zh: 我说极少数人，是因为虽然我偶尔也会这么做，而且我确实觉得这挺好玩、挺有意思，
cues.en: when I say few people, because I, although I do do this on occasion and I do think it's actually kind of fun and interesting,

cues.zh: 但对我写的大多数代码来说，我通常工作太多，根本没时间这么做。
cues.en: I usually have way too much work to do this for most of the code that I write.

cues.zh: 所以，如果你问我是否遵循这种优化哲学，我会说一年也就一次之类的，对吧？
cues.en: So, if you were to ask me if I follow this philosophy of optimization, I would say once a year or something, right?

cues.zh: 但大多数时候，我并不遵循那套优化哲学。
cues.en: But most of the time I'm not following that philosophy of optimization.

cues.zh: 第二点是：不做负优化。
cues.en: Um, number two is non-pessimization.

cues.zh: 不做负优化是一种理念：写代码时，我只写尽可能简单的东西
cues.en: Non-pessimization is a philosophy that says when I'm writing code, I'm just going to write the simplest possible thing

cues.zh: 不给 CPU 引入大量额外工作，这样总体上，
cues.en: and not introduce tons of extra work for the CPU to do, so that in general,

cues.zh: 我产出的代码至少不会做不必要的事，对吧？
cues.en: the code that I produce is at least not doing things unnecessarily, right?

cues.zh: 所以它其实和优化没那么像。
cues.en: So it's not really that similar to optimization.

cues.zh: 它不是去设想某件事应该跑多快、测量硬件的实际性能、收集详细的性能数据并比较，然后做修改，
cues.en: It's not about coming up with ideas about how fast something should run, measuring the actual performance of the hardware, taking detailed performance collection information and comparing it, and then making changes

cues.zh: 看看能不能，怎么说呢，基本上像做梯度下降一样，把代码调到跑得和你认为的差不多快。
cues.en: to see if you can sort of, you know, basically uh gradient descent down to code that runs about as fast as you think it should.

cues.zh: 这跟那个没关系。
cues.en: It's not about that.

cues.zh: 其实，我可能有一半时间根本都不去计时。
cues.en: In fact, I may not even be timing it half the time.

cues.zh: 关键在于别给计算机引入一大堆额外的工作。
cues.en: It's simply about not introducing tons of extra work for the computer to do.

cues.zh: 所以从很多方面来说，这几乎跟优化完全不相关。
cues.en: So in many ways, it's it's almost completely unrelated to optimization.

cues.zh: 它只是说，我永远不会主动往 CPU 里塞一堆代码，让它必须先啃完这些才能干真正的工作。
cues.en: It's just saying I'm never going to you know, willingly pile a bunch of code into the CPU that it has to chew through in order to get to the actual work.

cues.zh: 我会让事情保持简单、直接，只做我认为解决当前问题真正需要做的事。
cues.en: I'm going to keep things simple, straightforward, and only really doing the things that I think are involved in the problem I'm solving.

cues.zh: 对于不是职业程序员的人来说，这话听起来可能像是理所当然。
cues.en: Now, for people who aren't career programmers, that statement may sound like a no-brainer.

cues.zh: 实际上，几乎没人这么做。
cues.en: Actually, it is practiced almost nowhere.

cues.zh: 所以我几乎 100% 都是这么做的，可以说这就是我 99% 情况下的优化哲学。
cues.en: So I do this 100% of the time, pretty much, like I would say this is my philosophy of optimization 99% of the time.

cues.zh: 大多数地方并不这么做。
cues.en: Most places do not do this.

cues.zh: 他们只是堆上大量额外工作，不管是使用拖慢一切的解释器，还是用他们根本不知道在干什么、又慢的库，还是用大量构造
cues.en: They simply pile on tons of extra work, whether that means using an interpreter that slows everything down, whether that means uh using libraries that they don't know what they do, that are slow, whether that means using lots of constructs

cues.zh: 比如不必要的虚函数、多态之类的东西，或者不必要的拷贝和类
cues.en: such as, you know, unnecessary virtual functions and polymorphism and all these sorts of things, or unnecessary copies and classes

cues.zh: 还有字符串类等等，他们只是打着“这样可能更简单”的幌子，引入大量额外工作
cues.en: and string classes and all these things, they just introduce tons of extra work under the guys of it being maybe easier for them

cues.zh: 或者更正确、更干净，或者他们发明出来的某种构造，来说服自己应该这么做。
cues.en: or more correct or more clean or whatever construct they have invented to uh to convince themselves that they should be doing this.

cues.zh: 他们并不这么做，对吧？
cues.en: They they don't do this, right?

cues.zh: 他们不这么做。
cues.en: They don't do this.

cues.zh: 他们只是给 CPU 堆上近乎无限的工作量。
cues.en: They just pile on nearly infinite amount of work for the CPU to do.

cues.zh: 嗯，所以实际上，他们从没想过要确保自己不会给 CPU 增加额外工作。
cues.en: Um, so in effect, they are never thinking about making sure that they're not giving the CPU extra work to do.

cues.zh: 他们只是理所当然地认为，可以把所有这些工作都丢给下面，你懂的，谁知道呢，然后指望一切顺利。
cues.en: They just kind of assume that they can just dump all that work down there and, you know, who knows, and then hope for the best.

cues.zh: 嗯，所以，非悲观化是第二种优化哲学，
cues.en: Um, so, non-pessimization is the second philosophy of optimization,

cues.zh: 我觉得它非常有价值，甚至可以说，它是最缺失的一种。
cues.en: and I think it's a very valuable one, and if anything, it's the one that's most missing.

cues.zh: 它之所以最缺失，尤其是因为第一种优化在某种意义上总能靠少数硬核的人完成。
cues.en: It's most missing especially because the first one can always be done by a few hardcore people in some sense.

cues.zh: 你需要做这类优化的代码路径数量，可能并没有那么多
cues.en: The the number of code paths you need to do this kind of optimization on probably aren't that many

cues.zh: 在一个普通的软件里。
cues.en: in the normal piece of software.

cues.zh: 所以，如果你那，你知道，一千人的公司雇了 10 个能做这件事的人，那大概就够了。
cues.en: So if your, you know, company of a thousand people employs 10 people who can do this, that's probably enough.

cues.zh: 但如果另外那 990 个人不这么做，懂怎么做这件事的人再怎么帮你也无济于事。
cues.en: But if the other 990 are not doing this, there's nothing the people who know how to do this can possibly do to help you.

cues.zh: 因为会生成大量被劣化的代码，只会给 CPU 制造无穷无尽的工作量，所以没有哪个硬核优化专家能进来
cues.en: Because so much code will be generated that is pessimized and that just creates infinite amount of work for the CPU to do, no hardcore optimization expert is going to be able to come in

cues.zh: 把它们全修好；他们能修一点，但不可能全修，因为这很花时间。
cues.en: and fix it all, they can fix a little bit, but they can't fix it all because, you know, this takes time.

cues.zh: 第一条是迄今为止最难做到的。
cues.en: Number one is the hardest to do by far.

cues.zh: 就像我说的，我几乎一直在做第二条，可以说这是我 99% 情况下的优化哲学。
cues.en: Like I said, I do number two pretty much all the time, like I would say this is my philosophy of optimization 99% of the time.

cues.zh: 第一条我几乎从不做，对吧？
cues.en: I do number one hardly ever, right?

cues.zh: 因为它成本很高，而且老实说，配套工具也不太好，对吧？
cues.en: Because it's very expensive and honestly the tools for it are also not very good, right?

cues.zh: 所以这是两条，然后第三条是我所谓的伪优化。
cues.en: So those are two, and then number three is what I call fake optimization.

cues.zh: 你可以把这想成类似达克效应式优化之类的。
cues.en: Um, and you could think of this as maybe something along the lines of a Duning-Kruger optimization or something like this.

cues.zh: 就是人们在谈代码速度，却根本不知道自己在说什么。
cues.en: It's when people talk about the speed of code, but they have no idea what they're talking about.

cues.zh: 这种情况其实很常见，甚至在 Refterm 那件事里也发生过，网上还有人讨论。
cues.en: So this happens actually quite frequently, it even happened during the Refterm thing, uh, people talking about it online.

cues.zh: 这并不是真正有用的东西。
cues.en: And this is not an actual useful thing.

cues.zh: 实际上它非常适得其反。
cues.en: It's it's actually very counterproductive.

cues.zh: 所以，和前两种不同——它们是真正能带来更好、更快代码的优化哲学——我认为，
cues.en: So unlike these two, which are philosophies of optimization that actually lead to better code that runs more quickly, I would argue,

cues.zh: 第三种往好了说是中性，也就是其实没起什么作用；往坏了说是适得其反，因为它让人把时间花在其实无关紧要、甚至会让事情更糟的事情上。
cues.en: number three is at best neutral, meaning it doesn't really do anything, uh, or at worst counterproductive because it leads people to spend time doing things that actually don't matter or that makes things worse.

cues.zh: 伪优化就是人们会说这种话：“你不该替换 memcopy，我只是用了 Refterm 上有人提到的一种做法。”
cues.en: Fake optimization is when people say things like you shouldn't replace memcopy, I'm just using one that got said on Refterm,

cues.zh: 你不该替换 memcopy，因为我看到过一个 Google 的演示，说 memcopy 在某个特定场景下已经优化过了，所以不调用它反而更慢，对吧？
cues.en: you shouldn't replace memcopy because I saw a Google presentation that said that memcopy was optimized on this certain thing, so it's slower to not call it, right?

cues.zh: 这些都不算真正的陈述，没有任何意义。
cues.en: These are non-statements, they don't mean anything.

cues.zh: 这不过是某人把某次看到的东西说出来而已。
cues.en: They're just somebody saying something they saw one time.

cues.zh: 但任何真正做过优化的人都知道，性能快慢极其取决于具体场景。
cues.en: But as anyone who's actually ever done optimization number one knows, the speed of things is incredibly case specific.

cues.zh: 要从一个幻灯片演示里拿东西来用，是非常非常困难的，首先你甚至不知道做那个演示的人到底做对了没有，
cues.en: It is very, very difficult to take something from a slide presentation where a, you don't even know if the person who did that presentation actually did the right thing or not,

cues.zh: 然后把它套到另一个代码库上——你可能根本都没参与那个代码库，或者你参与了，但从没实际验证过你正在重复的那些优化
cues.en: and then apply it to some other code base that you're not even necessarily involved in or that you are involved in but you've never done the work to see whether or not the optimizations that you're repeating

cues.zh: 是否和你看过的东西具有同样的特性，对吧？
cues.en: have the same kind of characteristics as they have in in what you looked at, right?

cues.zh: 那个，呃，你知道，我不确定这事儿怎么表述最好，但有点像有些人谈论优化，可自己并不真正理解，
cues.en: So, uh, you know, I don't know what the best articulation for this is, but it's sort of like people who say things about optimization that they don't really understand,

cues.zh: 但这几乎像是一种模因式的重复，重复的东西也许最初来自某种优化哲学，比如某人真的做过测量。
cues.en: but it's almost like a memetic repeating of something that maybe once came from this philosophy of optimization, like that someone actually measured something.

cues.zh: 但重复它的人并不明白，真正做测量、真正去测试他们正在改的那条代码路径的过程，
cues.en: But the people repeating it don't understand that the measuring and the process of actually testing the code path they were working on

cues.zh: 才是让代码变快的部分，而不是他们说的那句话。
cues.en: is the part that led to the faster code, not the thing they said.

cues.zh: 另一个例子是“数组比链表快”。
cues.en: Another example of this is arrays are faster than linked lists.

cues.zh: 这同样是模因式重复，我几乎可以保证，对某个当时在给自己的代码计时的人来说，这话是真的。
cues.en: Again, it's a memetic repeating of something that I can almost guarantee was true for somebody who was timing something that they were doing.

cues.zh: 但这根本不算有效论断。
cues.en: But it's a non-statement.

cues.zh: 数组和链表是两种不同的策略，它们的性能差异巨大，取决于它们的内存布局，以及你的增删模式等等。
cues.en: Arrays and linked lists are two different strategies, their performance varies tremendously depending on how they are laid out as well and what your sort of growth deletion patterns are, all that sort of stuff.

cues.zh: 所以说“数组比链表快”这种话是无稽之谈，并不成立，它们是两种不同的算法，
cues.en: So saying something like arrays are faster than linked lists is a nonsense statement, it's not true, they are two different algorithms,

cues.zh: 有时这个更快，有时那个更快，取决于很多因素，对吧？
cues.en: sometimes one's faster, sometimes the other's faster, it depends on a lot of factors, right?

cues.zh: 所以伪优化是第三种优化哲学，而且是非常糟糕的一种。
cues.en: So fake optimization is the third philosophy and it's a very bad philosophy.

cues.zh: 呃，我们真的不该这么做，但你会经常看到它发生。
cues.en: Uh, it's one that we really shouldn't be doing but that you see happen a lot.

cues.zh: 更不幸的是，它出现的频率远远高于那两种真正有用的优化哲学。
cues.en: And what's really unfortunate is you see it happen way more often than the two philosophies of optimization that are actually useful.

cues.zh: 好，嗯，既然如此，我就简单讲一下，呃，我在做 Refterm 时发生了什么。
cues.en: Okay, um, so with that in mind, I'm just going to briefly sketch out what happened, uh, when I was working on Refterm.

cues.zh: Refterm 只是一个简单的项目，它只花了，我是说，总共可能也就六七天的编程时间。
cues.en: Refterm was just a simple project, it only took, I mean maybe the sum total of time on it was six or seven days of programming time.

cues.zh: 那个项目只是想实际演示一下，为什么事实是：如果你只是解决这个问题
cues.en: And that project was just to try and give an actual demonstration of why of the fact that if you were to just solve this problem

cues.zh: 用非常直接的方式，不往里面堆大量复杂代码，它就会运行得非常快。
cues.en: in a very straightforward way without dumping tons of complicated code into it, it would run very quickly.

cues.zh: 所以，有人说这不知怎么就是个难题，或者说它跑得不快，呃，或者说没法让它跑得快
cues.en: So the fact that people were suggesting that somehow this was a difficult problem or that it doesn't run quickly, uh, or that it can't be made to run quickly

cues.zh: 或者说需要付出极其艰巨的优化工作才能做到，这些说法都完全没有根据。
cues.en: or that it would take heroic optimization efforts to do so are simply unfounded.

cues.zh: 首先我要说的是，在这三者——优化、非悲观化和假优化——之中，呃，我真正用到的只有第二个。
cues.en: So the first thing I'll say is that of those three, optimization, non-pessimization and fake optimization, the, uh, really only one I used was number two.

cues.zh: 我在写 Refterm 参考光栅化器时所做的，就是让它比大多数终端程序渲染器快大约一千倍，呃，至少在所有情况下都快一百倍。
cues.en: All I did when writing the Refterm reference rasterizer, which was about a thousand times faster than most terminal program renderers were, uh, at least a hundred times faster in all cases.

cues.zh: 它更快的原因很简单：我只是坐下来，敲入了非悲观化的代码。
cues.en: The reason that that is faster is simply because I sat down and typed in code that was non-pessimized.

cues.zh: 就是这样。
cues.en: That's it.

cues.zh: 只有一个地方，我确实只是做了个东西，用来打印把整个缓冲区——比如我们整个巨大的数据集——灌进去要花多久，呃，这样我就能快速改几处
cues.en: There is one place, I literally just had a thing that would print out how long it took to sink an entire buffer of like our an entire giant uh data set to it, uh so that I could just do a couple quick changes

cues.zh: 来确保我在某个东西上能获得合理的吞吐量。
cues.en: to make sure that I was getting reasonable throughput on something.

cues.zh: 所以严格来说，那确实是我做过的一个实际优化任务。
cues.en: So that is technically a actual optimization task that I did.

cues.zh: 除了那个非常孤立的情况，其余一切都只是避免悲观化。
cues.en: Other than that one, very isolated thing, everything else was just non-pessimization.

cues.zh: 其余都只是敲入简单直接的写法，没有给 CPU 堆上一大堆额外工作。
cues.en: Everything else was just typing in the simple thing without piling on a ton of extra work for the CPU to do.

cues.zh: 所以当人们谈论这些时，嗯，我真的觉得他们漏掉了这种二分法。
cues.en: And so when people talk about these things, um, I really think they're missing this dichotomy.

cues.zh: 所以我想过一遍这到底是怎么运作的，并解释清楚，因为我想说明：其实当人们说“哦，你知道，优化就是太花时间了，我们做不到”时，或者说他们其实在想第一点——把优化看作硬核优化者才会做的真正工作——
cues.en: So I want to go over how this works and explain it because I want to show that actually what people are thinking when they say, oh like you know optimization, it just takes too much time, we wouldn't be able to do it or they're kind of thinking about that number one point, the optimization as a real thing that hardcore optimizers do

cues.zh: 他们会去看汇编语言，做所有这些事，数周期，看性能计数器里有多少 Uops 卡在什么环节上，对吧？
cues.en: where they're looking at the assembly language and they're doing all this stuff, and they're counting cycles and they're looking at performance counters for how many Uops were stalled on which thing, right?

cues.zh: 不。
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 这不是把需要放在那里的额外代码放进去，而是把不需要放在那里的代码也放进去。
cues.en: It's not putting extra code in there that needs to, that doesn't need to be in there.

cues.zh: 在我继续之前先说明一下，因为很多人会在某个时刻直接关掉视频然后去抱怨，因为他们在前半部分没有听到自己想听的内容，
cues.en: And before I go any further, because a lot of people will just shut this video off at some point and go complain about it because they didn't hear what they wanted to hear in the first part,

cues.zh: 向后兼容，或者诸如此类的借口
cues.en: backwards compatibility or other excuses like that

cues.zh: 真的就只是那样。
cues.en: are literally just that.

cues.zh: 它们就是借口。
cues.en: They're just excuses.

cues.zh: 向后兼容从来不是代码变慢的理由。
cues.en: Backwards compatibility is never a reason for code to be slow.

cues.zh: 实现向后兼容有很多方法，我在 Refterm 里实际演示了其中一些。
cues.en: There are many ways you can achieve backwards compatibility, I actually demonstrate some of those in Refterm.

cues.zh: 而且 Refterm 渲染器的一个有趣之处是，它在很多方面的能力实际上比我拿来对比的那些还要多。
cues.en: And one of the interesting things about the Refterm renderer is it actually has more capabilities in a lot of areas than the ones that I was actually comparing it to.

cues.zh: 所以我们可以做它们做不到的事。
cues.en: So we can do things that they can't do.

cues.zh: 我这么做的原因并不是要演示什么，因为我不认为 Refterm 是一个完整的终端实现；如果它是，我就会把它作为终端发布。我这么做是为了表明，实际上我能处理你想在这里加的任何情况。
cues.en: And the reason I did that was just not to demonstrate because I don't claim that Refterm is a full implementation of a terminal, if I did I'd ship it as a terminal, the reason I did that was to show that actually I can handle whatever cases you want in here.

cues.zh: 因为特殊情况、向后兼容，所有这些，其实都相当容易塞进流水线里，
cues.en: Because special cases, backwards compatibility, all that stuff, those are things that are actually fairly easy to slot into a pipeline,

cues.zh: 而且只要没被拖慢，它们真的花不了你多少成本。
cues.en: and if it's non-pessimized, they really don't cost you much.

cues.zh: 因为支持这些东西，你要做的不过是把这些情况隔离到较慢的路径里，对吧？
cues.en: Because all you ever do to support those things is you just isolate those cases into slower paths, right?

cues.zh: 发布一个在向后兼容路径上很慢的东西，完全没问题。
cues.en: It's totally fine to ship something that's slow on a back compat path.

cues.zh: 比如说，在一个终端程序里，它有一堆事情要做，而且一直都非常快。
cues.en: Like, let's say for example, in a terminal program, I have a bunch of things that it's doing, and it's really fast all the time.

cues.zh: 但然后你运行一个 1980 年的古老程序，你知道，它会稍微慢一点，运行那东西会慢上一倍，这完全没问题，因为它可能走了一条更慢的向后兼容路径，因为它检测到出现了那种情况，并对那种情况做了不同处理，对吧？
cues.en: But then you run some ancient program from 1980 and you know, it's a little bit slower, it's twice as slow running that thing, that's totally fine because maybe it's going down a slower backwards compatibility path because it detected that that case occurred and handles that one differently, right?

cues.zh: 这些都没问题，而且代码里经常发生。
cues.en: Those things are totally fine and they happen in code all the time.

cues.zh: 但你的 99% 场景是所有人都在用这个程序，而他们做的绝大多数事情并不需要那种向后兼容，拿这个当借口，说为什么你没法像那个显然快得多的方案一样快，
cues.en: But having your 99% case where everyone's using this program that doesn't need that backwards compatibility thing for the vast majority of things that they do, using that as an excuse as to why you can't be as fast as the obvious thing that is way faster,

cues.zh: 尤其当已经有人把它发到网上作为演示之后，那简直就只是个借口。
cues.en: especially once someone's already posted that on the internet as a demonstration, is literally just an excuse.

cues.zh: 这完全没有任何正当理由。
cues.en: And there's no justification for it, um, whatsoever.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 那我来讲讲 Refterm 的结构，我是怎么让它不被“劣化”的，
cues.en: So let me talk about the structure of Refterm, how I kept it non-pessimized,

cues.zh: 以及为什么我认为它跑得比很多其他情况快得多。
cues.en: um, and why I think that it runs so much faster than what you see in a lot of other cases.

cues.zh: 第一部分就到这里，希望你们喜欢。
cues.en: That's it for part one, I hope you enjoyed it.

cues.zh: 明天我会回来讲第二部分，在那之前，请看看我们的 Kickstarter，链接在下面的描述里。
cues.en: I'll be back here tomorrow with part two and until then, please check out our Kickstarter, the links in the description below.

cues.zh: 我们很想送你一本很酷的图像小说，所以请务必去看看。
cues.en: We'd love to send you a cool graphic novel, so please check it out.
